text: CLI script execution. doeff run can run a program, and then run a script of yours against that run.
First the program runs, and the effects it yields are answered by its handlers.
Then your script runs, with the program, its value, and its interpreter already in hand.
Here is the command: a program path, then a dash, so the script is read from standard input.
No interpreter is given, so doeff takes the closest marked one on the module path: checkout interpreter.
The default envs along the path are merged in order, and the closer one wins: the tax rate is zero point one.
checkout interpreter runs the program under a reader that holds the merged env.
Each Ask travels out to the reader, and its answer comes back to the yield.
The program returns forty six twenty euros. That is the value.
Now the script runs, and doeff has put five names in its globals.
value is what the program returned.
program is the program as it was imported, still a value you can run. interpreter is the one that ran it.
sys and json come along too. Anything else, the script imports itself.
Because program is a value, the script can run it again.
Give the interpreter another env, and the same Asks get new answers: fifty two fifty, in dollars.
Call it with no env, and nothing holds the tax rate. The Ask fails with a missing env key error.
The script can also wrap the program in handlers of its own.
trace receives each Ask, prints its key, and passes it on to the reader.
free answers the tax rate itself, with zero, and passes currency on.
Same program, other handlers, another meaning: forty two euros.
If the script raises, doeff prints the error and exits with status one.
What the script printed before the error stays on standard output.
doeff run runs your program with its handlers, then hands the run to your script, where the program is a value you can run again, under any handlers.
